claims.text: Mg-transition-metal alloys experience an intermediate-temperature regime in which local chemical ordering drives phase segregation and microstructural instability.
Mg volatility becomes problematic above 1000 °C.
A rapid ramp to 850 °C initiates solid-state diffusion without causing excessive local chemical ordering.
A 60-minute dwell at 920 °C promotes formation of a single-phase solid solution through high-configurational-entropy stabilization.
Cooling at 5 °C/min suppresses formation of brittle ordered domains.
Adding 2–4 at.% Al and 3–5 at.% Cr produces a continuous, self-healing mixed Al2O3/Cr2O3 layer in the proposed Mg alloy.
The mixed Al2O3/Cr2O3 layer is thermodynamically stable in the 850–920 °C processing regime.
Protective alumina and chromia layers act as diffusion barriers against further oxidation.
The proposed oxide layer prevents Mg dissolution and transition-metal segregation.
Sintering below 800 °C provides insufficient diffusion, causing relative density below 95% and porosity above 5%.
Above 1000 °C, Mg vapor pressure exceeds 10 Pa and Mg loss exceeds 5%, causing porosity and composition drift.
Microstructural segregation peaks between 850 and 950 °C when dwell time exceeds 60 minutes.
Standard sintering at 950 °C for two hours produces only 85% relative density.
Standard sintering at 950 °C for two hours causes 5 wt% Mg loss.
Standard sintering at 950 °C produces a multiphase microstructure with segregated transition-metal clusters.
The proposed thermal profile will produce relative density above 98% and porosity below 2%.
The proposed process will produce an HCP single-phase-like solid solution containing less than 5% secondary phase.
The alloy will exhibit oxidation weight gain below 0.5 mg/cm² after 100 hours at 900 °C.
The alloy will exhibit a corrosion rate below 0.1 mm/year in neutral salt spray.
The alloy will exhibit Vickers hardness above 150 HV.

contradictions.description: The volatility boundary is presented as above 1000 °C, but the baseline simultaneously attributes significant 5 wt% Mg loss to sintering at 950 °C.

The process is said to avoid prolonged residence in the ordering-prone regime, yet it includes 90 minutes of total dwell at 850 and 920 °C, while the stated boundary says segregation peaks over 850–950 °C for dwell times exceeding 60 minutes.
The boundary defines dominant volatility as more than 5% Mg loss above 1000 °C, whereas the falsification rule uses more than 3% Mg loss at exactly 1000 °C.
